items.content_html:
Resolves #445117, supersedes #401080 & #449578.

K3s and RKE2 share a lot of functionality, but since the nixpkgs RKE2 maintainer team is much smaller than K3s', its module tends to fall far behind - and for feature parity, code duplication across the two modules would be needed (see #401080). Merging them should make it possible for the RKE2 module to keep up with K3s without having maintainers manually copy code over.

I haven't removed or added any options, this PR is more or less just a (big) refactor. I also haven't tested the K3s module manually, but all tests in nixos/tests/{k3s,rke2} passed and I'm currently using the RKE2 module to host my site with no issues.

I've also added myself as a maintainer to RKE2.

Maintainer cc:
@rorosen @zimbatm @stefan-bordei
@NixOS/k3s

In my case the closure was already symlinked and when the activation service ran before switching root, it would fail, causing the system to not be able to leave the first stage, saying "Switch root target does not contain usable init".

On regular, mutable NixOS systems this is usually not an issue, however, when building read-only images where /nix/store is mounted to /sysroot/nix/store, edge cases like this are more likely to happen.

items.title: nixos/hydroxide: init module

items.content_html:
Problem Statement

The etesync-dav service module has several hard-coded elements:

  1. The etesync-dav package is pinned to use pkgs.etesync-dav by default.
  2. The name of the data directory that the service module uses is hard-coded to be /var/lib/etesync-dav.

Resolution

This PR extends this service module by adding user options to make it more declarative:

  1. A services.etesync-dav.package option that defaults to pkgs.etesync-dav allows the user to choose a different version/patch of etesync-dav.
  2. A services.etesync-dav.dataDir option that defaults to /var/lib/etesync-dav allows the user to choose the name of the data directory, whilst also exposing it as a configuration variable that can be accessed in other modules.

items.content_html:
NixOS containers currently copy the /etc/resolv.conf from the host to the guest indiscriminantly. When using features like extraFlags = ["--network-namespace-path=/run/netns/..."] this can cause the container to have completely broken DNS, as it can copy a resolv.conf that specifies a resolver running on localhost when that resolver is inaccessible.

Add an option copyResolvConf to NixOS containers that defaults to true (the existing behaviour) and decides whether to copy the resolv.conf from the host. This allows running containers using a network namespace that contains only a wireguard interface, for example.

I've been using this feature for close to a year now and it works well. Please let me know if it would be appropriate to add tests for this - I think it will end up being quite a niche feature but is extremely useful.
